cards.text: The LORD is speaking through Hosea, His prophet, and He's laying out a charge against His people. First up is Ephraim, another name here for the house of Israel. And friend, what comes next is NOT a compliment.

cards.question: The LORD says Ephraim surrounds Him with something. What is it?

cards.text: So Ephraim is wrapping God up in lies, and the house of Israel in deceit. Then the LORD mentions Judah, the other kingdom of His people.

cards.question: The LORD says Judah still walks with God and is faithful to the Holy One.

cards.text: Back to Ephraim. He feeds on the wind and chases the east wind all day long. That's me in a parking lot chasing a receipt that is NOT coming back.

cards.question: Ephraim multiplies lies and violence. He makes a covenant with ___ and sends olive oil to ___.

cards.text: Ephraim is chasing wind and cutting deals. Then the LORD says He has a charge to bring.

cards.question: The LORD's charge leaves Judah out.

cards.text: He will punish Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds. Then the LORD goes all the way back to Jacob himself, the forefather of His people, before he was even born.

cards.question: Jacob's grabbing starts early. While he's still in the womb, what does he grab?

cards.text: When Jacob is grown and strong, he wrestles with God. He struggles with the angel and prevails, and friend, I once lost a wrestling match to a twist tie. TWICE.

cards.question: Jacob just won his wrestling match with the angel. What does he do?

answers.text: He weeps and seeks God's favor
He walks off without a word

cards.question: Jacob found God at ___ and spoke with Him there.

cards.text: Then the passage stops to name exactly who Jacob met there: "the LORD God of Hosts, the LORD is His name of renown."
Now the LORD turns from Jacob's story to His people right now. Jacob wept and sought His favor, so what about them?

cards.question: What does the LORD tell His people they must do?
The LORD tells His people to maintain love and justice and to wait on Him only when times get hard.

cards.text: Then the LORD points at a merchant who loves to cheat with dishonest scales in his hands. That's like me calling a cookie the size of a hubcap ONE serving.

cards.question: Right after the dishonest merchant, Ephraim starts boasting. What does Ephraim brag about?
Ephraim claims no one can find any sinful iniquity in him.

cards.text: But the LORD answers that brag. He's been their God ever since the land of Egypt.

cards.question: Rich Ephraim is in for a change. The LORD says He will again make them dwell in ___, as in the days of the appointed feast.

cards.text: And His people can't say nobody warned them. The LORD multiplied visions and gave parables.

cards.question: Who did the LORD speak through to give His people those visions and parables?

cards.text: Then the LORD calls out two places. Is there iniquity in Gilead? They will surely come to nothing.

cards.question: In Gilgal they sacrifice bulls. What does the LORD say their altars will become?

answers.text: Heaps of stones in the field

cards.text: Then the LORD brings up Jacob one more time. Jacob flees to the land of Aram, and I envy that, friend, because every getaway I make is a HOP with a gold base attached.

cards.question: In Aram, Jacob, also called Israel, tends sheep. What is he working for?
Jacob ran off and worked for what he got. But the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt by a ___.
The LORD also preserved Israel by a prophet.

cards.text: And the LORD wraps it up with Ephraim. Ephraim has provoked bitter anger.

cards.question: Ephraim has provoked bitter anger. What will his Lord leave upon him?

cards.text: And his Lord will repay him for his contempt. That's the charge, friend, laid out start to finish.

findings.problem: The setup says what comes next is "NOT a compliment." That rules out the wrong answer "Praise", and probably "Gifts", on card 2, so only "Lies" is left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 4 just established that Judah still walks with God and is faithful. Card 7 gives no context about Judah. A thoughtful baker would reason that the charge leaves Judah out and pick True. Getting this right means going against the earlier cards, not reasoning from them.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The card cites only Hosea 12:2. It also tells that the LORD goes back to Jacob "before he was even born," which comes from Hosea 12:3.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "He demands a big reward" is close to Jacob demanding a blessing from the one he wrestled (Genesis 32:26). A baker who knows that story could argue it is right alongside "He weeps and seeks God's favor."

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: "Jacob just won his wrestling match" adds that the weeping came immediately after he prevailed. Hosea 12:4 lists the two actions but gives no timing between them.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: "Rich Ephraim is in for a change" ties the boast in 12:8 to the tents in 12:9 and frames dwelling in tents as a consequence of the riches. The text doesn't say how the two connect. The framing also helps rule out "palaces."

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "His people can't say nobody warned them" adds a reason for the visions and parables, namely that they were warnings. Hosea 12:10 doesn't say why the LORD spoke through the prophets.

rule.text: Reasons. He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The card is a bare paraphrase of the verse with none of Papa Dorin's voice. It says "two places" but names only Gilead.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card is a bare restatement of the verse with no voice. Card 15's question then repeats the same line, so this card adds almost nothing.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 5 of the 9 choice cards, against 2 true or false and 2 fill in the blank. The stop also opens with the same type pattern as stop 1: multiple choice, then true or false, then fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Several lines in the passage speak of the LORD in the third person, so the prophet seems to be speaking: 12:2 "The LORD has a charge", 12:6 "return to your God", 12:13 "the LORD brought Israel" and 12:14 "his Lord will leave". The cards present these as the LORD speaking: stop 1 cards 7 and 15, and stop 2 cards 10 and 14. The "Who's speaking" rule only covers quotes in the first person.
findings.question: In prophetic passages, can lines that refer to the LORD in the third person be presented as the LORD speaking, because card 1 says He speaks through the prophet? Or should Papa Dorin attribute them to the prophet, or leave the speaker open?
